1 # AgentForge AI 2 3 4 5 AgentForge is a chat with one honest agent: a system prompt and a set of tools. 6 It answers directly, researches the web, reads and edits code in a sandbox, and 7 replies in plain text. The reply is shown exactly as the model wrote it. Nothing 8 grades it, wraps it in a status or limits how long it works; a provider's own 9 error is shown as it is, and Stop ends a run. See [the agent](docs/agent.md). 10 11 Coding runs in a persistent E2B sandbox per conversation (internet on, no 12 secrets inside). In **Ask me** mode the agent stops before anything that changes 13 something (a command, a file write or edit, a pull request) and the chat shows an 14 Approve / Decline card with exactly what will happen: the command, the file content 15 or edit, or the pull request's changed files. In **Approve for me** mode it never asks. Each task keeps 16 event history and a usage ledger. 17 18 The workspace supports persistent conversations and immutable custom-agent 19 versions. GitHub App sign-in uses durable, revocable sessions and retains the 20 user's own repository permissions. See [implementation status](phase-status.md) 21 and [qualification tracker](docs/remaining-phases.md) for tested boundaries. 22 23 Start a conversation and describe the work. The composer has an optional 24 repository selection that defaults to No repo, and the Ask me / Approve for me 25 switch. The sidebar focuses on conversations. Account, GitHub, conversation 26 and appearance preferences and custom-agent management live in Settings; plugins and skills have their own Plugins page. See 27 [conversation behavior and migration](docs/conversation-ux.md) for the details. 28 Plugins (remote MCP servers the person connects, chosen per conversation from the composer) are described in 29 [plugins](docs/plugins.md). Skills (built-in and the person's own playbooks, loaded when a request fits or 30 asked for with `/name`) are described in [skills](docs/skills.md). 31 Durable queued follow-ups, source-linked conversation summaries, original-input 32 retrieval and deployment requirements are documented in 33 [conversation reliability](docs/conversation-reliability.md). 34 Every run can be traced to Neatlogs (model and tool calls, tokens, cost, retries, failures and 35 approvals, grouped per conversation); by default no prompt or answer leaves the worker. See 36 [Neatlogs tracing](docs/neatlogs.md). 37 38 ```mermaid 39 flowchart LR 40 Browser --> Proxy[Same-origin TLS proxy] 41 Proxy --> Web[Next.js workspace] 42 Proxy --> API[FastAPI identity and task API] 43 API --> DB[(PostgreSQL tasks, events, leases)] 44 Worker[Python worker] --> DB 45 Worker --> Agent[Agent loop: model, tools, plain-text answer] 46 Agent --> Providers[Configured model and research adapters] 47 Agent --> E2B[Persistent E2B sandbox per conversation] 48 Agent --> Approvals[Inline approval cards in the chat] 49 Worker --> Artifacts[Private POSIX artifact storage] 50 API --> Artifacts 51 Worker --> GitHub[Draft pull requests, opened by the backend] 52 ``` 53 54 ## Development 55 56 Use Python 3.12–3.13, uv, Node 24 and pnpm **10.34.6** (via corepack), with a local 57 PostgreSQL server. Dependencies are locked in `apps/api/uv.lock` and 58 `apps/web/pnpm-lock.yaml`. 59 60 ```sh 61 scripts/dev-setup.sh # checks tools, creates .env from .env.example if absent, installs dependencies 62 # edit .env: DATABASE_URL and the LLM_* block 63 (cd apps/api && uv run alembic upgrade head) # or: scripts/dev-setup.sh --migrate 64 (cd apps/api && uv run python -m agentforge.auth.bootstrap --write-env) # local sign-in 65 (cd apps/api && uv run python -m agentforge.doctor) # PASS/FAIL per requirement 66 scripts/dev.sh # API :8000, worker and web :3000 together; Ctrl-C stops all 67 ``` 68 69 Open `http://localhost:3000` (the landing page), choose **Get started** or **Sign in**, and enter the 70 `LOCAL_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN` from `.env`. The public pages (`/`, `/sign-in`, `/sign-up`) and the workspace 71 (`/chat`, `/settings`) are described in [conversation behavior](docs/conversation-ux.md#urls). For a 72 deployment, set `SITE_URL` (the public origin) at build time so the social card, sitemap and robots use it. 73 Configuration lives in an ignored root `.env`, kept to what you must set; 74 [.env.example](.env.example) is the template, [docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md) 75 lists every other setting with its default, and [Settings](apps/api/src/agentforge/settings.py) 76 is the contract. The API refuses to start on invalid settings and names the fields, never their 77 values. Never overwrite an existing `.env` with the template. For GitHub sign-in 78 and private repositories, create a GitHub App as in [docs/github-app.md](docs/github-app.md). 79 Set `E2B_API_KEY` for the coding sandbox and `EXA_API_KEY` for web search (`TAVILY_API_KEY` works as the fallback, or on its own). 80 `API_ORIGIN` (in `apps/web/.env.local`, default `http://localhost:8000`) is the 81 server-only origin of Next.js's API rewrite; deployments route `/api/` directly 82 to FastAPI on the same origin. 83 84 ## Checks and release 85 86 From the repository root: 87 88 ```sh 89 uv run --project apps/api python scripts/release_checks.py 90 ``` 91 92 This runs unit checks, uniquely named disposable PostgreSQL fixtures and frontend 93 lint/types/build. It writes private logs and a machine-readable receipt under 94 ignored `.local/releases/`. The local PostgreSQL OS-user administrator needs 95 CREATE DATABASE, or use `TEST_DATABASE_ADMIN_URL` naming the loopback administrative 96 `postgres` database. Fixtures migrate and remove only their newly created database; 97 they do not upgrade the configured application database or call paid providers. 98 Use pnpm 10.34.6; a global pnpm 12 installation is incompatible with this lockfile. 99 100 [Phase 7](docs/phase-7.md) maps golden fixtures to actual evidence and open gates. 101 [Single-EC2 deployment](infra/deploy/README.md) includes TLS, nonroot app services, 102 least-privilege runtime database access, persistent encrypted disk requirements, 103 backups, restore and restart procedures. Container execution and AWS deployment 104 remain unqualified until run on a deployment host. This is a single-instance 105 release configuration, with downtime during coordinated backups and no HA claim. 106 107 [Hackathon evidence](docs/hackathon.md) provides the partner-evidence checklist, 108 demo script and business-plan assumptions. A local fixture receipt is not live 109 provider evidence or a completed submission. 110

commit 7d33f8cd915b4ee334b3550f0efbc89b4d1811bd
Author: Harsh Kolte <74823522+harshkolte01@users.noreply.github.com>
Date:   Mon Oct 12 00:30:28 2026 +0530

    Make the Neatlogs integration complete and verified against the real SDK
    
    The existing integration traced runs but, checked against the SDK's own
    behaviour, lost most of what the dashboard reads and hid failures:
    
    - The export mask ran after the SDK normalised attributes, so its allowlist
      dropped neatlogs.llm.token_count.*, the model name, session id and tags:
      no token counts, model or cost reached Neatlogs. cost_usd was never mapped
      to the field the backend reads.
    - SDK trace() does not record exceptions, and spawn_subagent reports failure
      as a returned result, so failed tools, models and agent runs looked OK.
    - Turns of a conversation were unrelated traces (no session grouping).
    - Refused calls, approvals, provider retries and context preparation were not
      visible at all.
    
    Changes
    - Mask: allowlist rebuilt from what the SDK actually exports; exception events
      keep their type only; own labels live under agentforge.*.
    - Spans: model (tokens, cost, provider, finish reason, retries), tool (cost,
      evidence, ERROR with the tool's code), agent (ERROR when the run failed),
      guardrail spans for "Ask me" approvals and refused calls, a prepare_context
      stage, and a task root carrying its final status and tool-failure count.
    - Sessions: conversation = Neatlogs session, person = end user; tags for env,
      release, model and NEATLOGS_TAGS (for before/after comparisons).
    - Settings: NEATLOGS_ENDPOINT, _TAGS, _SAMPLE_RATE, _CAPTURE_CONTENT. Content
      capture is opt-in, with secret masking and size limits; the default stays
      metadata-only.
    - Resilience: an SDK that cannot start no longer stops the worker; spans never
      raise into a run; shutdown flushes then closes once with a 10 s bound.
    - Adapter: optional on_attempt_failed hook so provider retries are counted.
    - Operations: doctor "neatlogs" line, configuration flag, SDK doctor in
      release checks, deployment env example, docs/neatlogs.md (trace map,
      privacy modes, verification, before/after and failure-recovery procedure).
    
    Verification
    - tests/test_neatlogs_wire.py runs the real SDK against a local OTLP receiver
      and decodes what would be sent; examples/neatlogs_trace_smoke.py does the
      same through the real worker, a throwaway Postgres and the real runner.
    - Full API suite: same 21 pre-existing Windows failures as clean HEAD, +54 new
      passing tests. All disposable-database fixtures pass.
    - No hosted trace was produced from this change.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

1	# Hackathon evidence pack
2	
3	Checked against [official neatHack requirements](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon)
4	on 10 October 2026. Code-only preparation is complete here; partner-account work,
5	deployment, recording and posting remain outstanding. **This is not a submission.**
6	
7	The published window starts 10 October at 12:30 IST, with submissions opening
8	12 October at 19:00 IST and a planned close around 23:55 IST; the final cutoff is
9	announced on Discord. Do not alter commit dates or imply pre-window code is
10	eligible. The official requirements call for Neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai evidence,
11	a public repository and a video no longer than three minutes. A quote-post draft
12	does not submit the entry.
13	
14	## Evidence manifest
15	
16	| Claim | Artifact to attach | Current state |
17	|---|---|---|
18	| Substantial task completes with evidence | Actual task receipt, source/test evidence and artifact download | Offline fixtures available; live end-to-end pending |
19	| Failure recovery works | Disclosed failing attempt and subsequent legitimate action | Actual generated fixture exits available; live trace pending |
20	| Neatlogs improved the agent | Before/after hosted trace links, comparable latency/tokens/cost and change | Integration implemented; hosted traces confirmed arriving (12 Oct, `docs/neatlogs.md`); before/after comparison runs still to do |
21	| Entire used during implementation | Allowed checkpoint + commit or actual versioned entire-graph output | Pending; no conversation/transcript export authorized |
22	| Business plan uses cfo.ai | Export/screenshots covering pricing, costs, revenue and runway | Assumption template below; cfo.ai export pending |
23	| Built in public | Actual dated #neatHack posts | Pending |
24	| Submitted | Public quote of official post with team/name/project/repo/demo | Pending; follow confirmed cutoff |
25	
26	Keep raw traces, user repositories and credentials private. Review screenshots
27	and exported graph/source snippets before public inclusion. By default the
28	application sends trace metadata only (structure, timing, tokens, cost, status);
29	`NEATLOGS_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true` adds prompts and tool data with best-effort secret
30	masking, which makes the inputs/responses visible in a demo trace. Still inspect
31	actual exports before sharing. Do not substitute a
32	mocked-provider receipt for hosted evidence.
33	
34	## Neatlogs evidence
35	
36	How the trace maps to each thing the official page asks to trace, how to run a before/after comparison with
37	`NEATLOGS_TAGS`, how to produce a failure-recovery trace, and what has and has not been verified are in
38	[neatlogs.md](neatlogs.md). Offline checks (`python -m neatlogs doctor --local`, `tests/test_neatlogs_wire.py`,
39	`examples/neatlogs_trace_smoke.py`) prove what would be exported; only a run with a real project key produces the hosted
40	trace links this pack needs. Record the worker's `neatlogs_trace_id=` log line for each run you want to cite.
41	
42	## Entire graph without transcript export
43	
44	The [official Entire Graph project](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph)
45	documents local static analysis and `entire graph health --repo . --json`. After
46	an operator installs a verified CLI/plugin, record `entire graph version`, the
47	commit being analyzed, and actual health/query output for a code question such as
48	approval reconciliation or worker lease fencing. Keep original output; do not
49	claim a graph/checkpoint has been produced before running the command. Do not run
50	`init-agents` merely for evidence: it writes repository guidance and should be a
51	separate intentional integration. No chat transcripts are needed for graph-only
52	code analysis.
53	
54	## Business-plan assumptions for cfo.ai
55	
56	Export internal cost aggregates with:
57	
58	```sh
59	cd apps/api
60	uv run python -m agentforge.operations.business_metrics --days 7 --output /secure-path/agentforge-costs.json
61	```
62	
63	This performs SELECT-only aggregation across application users and creates a new
64	mode-0600 file. It exports task counts and measured/conservative ledger costs;
65	unknown operation costs retain their recorded upper bound. No goals, prompts,
66	user/task IDs, repository names, artifact content or secrets are included. It is
67	operator-only business evidence, **not** a provider invoice or cfo.ai export.
68	
69	Enter these explicit assumptions into cfo.ai, using measured results where
70	available and labeling every unmeasured value:
71	
72	| Input | Evidence/value source |
73	|---|---|
74	| Monthly price and included task allowance | Product hypothesis; choose after measured task distribution |

83	measured cost/task. Gross margin = (revenue − variable costs − hosting costs −

1	# Neatlogs tracing
2	
3	Every task the worker runs is traced to [Neatlogs](https://docs.neatlogs.com) when `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` is set. This page says
4	what is recorded, what is never sent, how to configure it, how to check it, and how to use it to improve the agent.
5	
6	Sources: the [Python SDK](https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/python), [sessions](https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/sessions),
7	[span kinds](https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/span-kinds), [lifecycle](https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/lifecycle),
8	[SDK Doctor](https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/doctor) and the [MCP server](https://docs.neatlogs.com/integrations/mcp), checked
9	against the published `neatlogs` 1.4.26 wheel on 12 October 2026. The neatHack requirement is to trace every agent run: model
10	and tool calls, inputs and responses, state changes, retries, failures, agent messages, latency, token usage and cost. The
11	table below maps each of those to where it appears.
12	
13	## What a trace contains
14	
15	One trace per task (a task is one chat turn). Turns of a conversation are one **session**.
16	
17	```
18	agentforge_task                      WORKFLOW   session = conversation, end user = person, tags, final status
19	├─ prepare_context                   CHAIN      history compaction / summary for this turn
20	└─ agent:builtin/agent               AGENT      the run; ERROR when the run failed, even though it returned a result
21	   ├─ <langgraph node>               CHAIN      LangGraph callback handler: graph steps
22	   ├─ model_request                  LLM        model, provider, tokens, cost, finish reason, retries
23	   ├─ tool_approval                  GUARDRAIL  "Ask me" decision: passed / blocked (the wait is the span's duration)
24	   ├─ tool_policy                    GUARDRAIL  a call refused before it ran (scope, schema, budget …) with its code
25	   ├─ web_search / bash / write …    TOOL       one per call; ERROR with the tool's code when it failed
26	   └─ agent:builtin/agent            AGENT      a delegated subagent, nested under the `delegate_task` TOOL span
27	```
28	
29	| Hackathon requirement | Where it is in the trace |
30	|---|---|
31	| Model calls | `model_request` (LLM): `neatlogs.llm.model_name`, `.provider`, `.token_count.prompt/completion/total`, `.cost_usd`, `.choices.0.finish_reason`; `agentforge.llm.messages`, `.tools_offered`, `.tool_calls`, `.cost_known`, `.reported_model` |
32	| Tool calls | one `TOOL` span per call: `tool.name`, `status`, `agentforge.tool.cost_usd`, `.evidence_count`, `.artifact_count` |
33	| Inputs and responses | content mode only (below); otherwise sizes and counts only |
34	| State changes | `agentforge.task.status` on the root; LangGraph node spans; `prepare_context`; `agentforge.agent.depth` / `.parent_run_id` |
35	| Retries | `agentforge.llm.retries` and `.retry_reasons` (rate limit, 5xx, timeout, broken stream); a tool that is retried by the model is a second `TOOL` span |
36	| Failures | span status `ERROR` + `agentforge.error.code` / `.type` on the failing span; an exception event whose type is the failure's code (`FETCH_COMPRESSED_CONTENT_REJECTED`, `RATE_LIMIT` …), never its text; shown by Neatlogs as the span's error type; the root is `ERROR` when the task failed |
37	| Failure recovery | root `agentforge.task.tool_failures` > 0 with `agentforge.task.status` = `COMPLETED`: the run hit failures and finished. The failing span is followed by the spans the agent chose next |
38	| Agent messages | the `AGENT` span per run and its parent link (`agentforge.agent.parent_run_id`); text only in content mode |
39	| Latency | span duration (`neatlogs.metrics.duration_ms`); the approval wait is its own span, separate from tool time |
40	| Tokens and cost | tokens per `LLM` span, summed per trace by Neatlogs. Neatlogs prices cost itself from its own model table (see Limits); AgentForge's ledger is the authoritative cost. An unknown cost is `agentforge.llm.cost_known = false`, never `0` |
41	| Guardrails | `tool_approval` / `tool_policy`: `neatlogs.guardrail.passed`, `.name`, `.reason` |
42	
43	Run ids tie a trace to the database: `spawn_id` on an `AGENT`/`TOOL` span is the `agent_runs.id`, `task_id` is `tasks.id`, and
44	the session id is the conversation id. The worker also logs `neatlogs_trace_id=<id>` for each task at INFO.
45	
46	## What is sent
47	
48	| Mode | Setting | Sent | Never sent |
49	|---|---|---|---|
50	| **metadata** (default) | `NEATLOGS_CAPTURE_CONTENT=false` | structure, timing, model, tokens, cost, status, error codes, tags, session and end-user ids, tool names | prompts, answers, tool arguments and results, repository text, URLs, exception messages and stacks, logs |
51	| **content** | `NEATLOGS_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true` | the above plus prompts, replies, tool arguments/results, LangGraph state; each value cut at 6000 characters; known secret shapes and every configured secret value masked | exception stacks, status text, logs |
52	
53	The rule is enforced by one export mask (`telemetry/neatlogs_setup.py`) that runs on every span after the SDK normalises its
54	attributes, so a callback or a new attribute cannot widen it: anything not on the allowlist (or under `agentforge.`) is dropped
55	in metadata mode. Content mode redacts on a best-effort basis (API-key shapes, bearer tokens, private keys, URL credentials,
56	`password=`/`token:` pairs, JWTs, and the exact secrets in the settings). **It is not a guarantee**; turn it on only for demos
57	and debugging, on data you are willing to share, and review a trace before publishing a screenshot. The end-user id is the
58	person's internal id; no name, email or GitHub login is sent.
59	
60	## Configuration
61	
62	| Variable | Default | Meaning |
63	|---|---|---|
64	| `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` | unset | Project key. Unset: nothing is traced and nothing is imported. |
65	| `NEATLOGS_WORKFLOW_NAME` | `agentforge-ai` | Names the application in the dashboard. Keep it stable across deployments. |
66	| `NEATLOGS_ENDPOINT` | SDK default | Base URL only (no path), e.g. `https://eu.ingest.neatlogs.com` for an EU project. |
67	| `NEATLOGS_TAGS` | empty | Comma-separated labels (max 10, 64 chars each) added to every trace, e.g. `baseline`, `prompt-v3`. |
68	| `NEATLOGS_SAMPLE_RATE` | `1` | Share of traces exported. Keep `1` when collecting evidence. |
69	| `NEATLOGS_CAPTURE_CONTENT` | `false` | See above. |
70	
71	`env:<APP_ENV>`, `release:<version>` and `model:<LLM_MODEL>` tags are always added; `user.id` is `agentforge-worker` (the
72	service, not a person). Tracing is **never allowed to stop a run**: if the SDK cannot start the worker logs an error and
73	runs untraced; a span that cannot be opened or closed is logged and skipped; attributes that cannot be set are ignored. On
74	shutdown the worker stops claiming tasks, lets running ones finish (or records them interrupted), then flushes and closes the
75	SDK once, each step bounded to 10 seconds (never a flush per request, as the SDK lifecycle guide asks).
76	
77	## Checking it
78	
79	Offline, no key, no network:
80	
81	```sh
82	cd apps/api
83	uv run python -m neatlogs doctor --local --json        # the installed SDK produces a valid local trace (also run by release_checks.py)
84	uv run python -m agentforge.doctor                      # "neatlogs" line: on/off, SDK version, metadata or content
85	uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_neatlogs*.py" -v
86	uv run python examples/neatlogs_trace_smoke.py          # real worker + real SDK + throwaway Postgres + a local OTLP receiver
87	```
88	
89	`tests/test_neatlogs_wire.py` and the smoke fixture run the *real* SDK against a receiver on 127.0.0.1 and decode exactly what
90	would be sent: tokens, cost, model, session grouping, error status, parent/child structure, and the absence of prompts and
91	secrets in metadata mode.
92	
93	Against the hosted project (needs the key; sends a synthetic trace; do not paste the key into logs):
94	
95	```sh
96	export NEATLOGS_API_KEY=...        # from your shell or secret store, never a committed file
97	cd apps/api && uv run python -m neatlogs doctor --probe --json
98	```
99	
100	A Doctor pass shows the SDK and key work; it does not show that this application's trace is right. Run one real task with
101	the worker and open its trace: one root, `agentforge_task`, in the conversation's session, with the tree above.
102	
103	## Using Neatlogs to improve the agent
104	
105	The loop the hackathon asks for is *measure, change one thing, measure again, keep the evidence*.
106	
107	1. **Baseline.** Start the worker with `NEATLOGS_TAGS=baseline`, run a fixed set of tasks (same prompts), note the trace ids
108	   from the worker log.
109	2. **Find the problem.** In the dashboard filter by `baseline` and sort by cost or duration; open the worst trace. Look for
110	   repeated `ERROR` spans, `tool_policy` refusals (the model is calling tools wrongly), `agentforge.llm.retries`, and many
111	   `model_request` spans (`agentforge.llm.messages` growing means context pressure).
112	3. **Or ask your coding agent.** The Neatlogs MCP server lets it read traces, detections and fix suggestions directly:
113	
114	   ```json
115	   { "mcpServers": { "neatlogs": { "type": "http", "url": "https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp",
116	       "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${NEATLOGS_API_KEY}" } } } }
117	   ```
118	
119	   (`.mcp.json` for Claude Code, `.cursor/mcp.json` for Cursor, or `npx @neatlogs/wizard mcp --api-key <key>`. Keep the key in
120	   the environment. Use the EU host for an EU project. Not run or verified in this repository.)
121	4. **Change one thing** (a prompt, a tool description, a budget) and restart the worker with `NEATLOGS_TAGS=improved`.
122	5. **Compare** the same tasks: tokens, cost, duration, error spans, and `agentforge.task.tool_failures` per task. Save both
123	   trace links (or screenshots) with the numbers; that is the before/after evidence.
124	
125	A **failure-recovery** example: run a task that makes the agent hit a real failure (for instance ask it to read a file that
126	does not exist, or decline an "Ask me" approval). In the trace the failing `TOOL`/`tool_policy`/`tool_approval` span is `ERROR`
127	or blocked, the next span is what the agent did instead, and the root ends `COMPLETED` with `tool_failures` > 0.
128	
129	## Verified against a hosted project
130	
131	Run on 12 October 2026 with a real project key (worker, API and web started locally, real model and search calls): the SDK
132	doctor probe passed; two conversations' tasks arrived as one trace each, grouped under the conversation's session, with the
133	tree above, per-call model, provider and token counts, tool spans, and `ERROR` spans for real tool failures carrying their
134	code as the error type. In one run the agent hit two `FETCH_COMPRESSED_CONTENT_REJECTED` failures and still finished with an
135	answer, which is the failure-recovery trace to cite. Read a trace back with
136	`GET <endpoint>/api/traces/v3/<trace id>` and the `x-api-key` header (what the SDK doctor does).
137	
138	## Limits
139	
140	- **Cost shows as "unpriced" for a model Neatlogs does not know.** Neatlogs computes cost server side from its model table and
141	  does not take the cost we send (`neatlogs.llm.cost_usd`; the hosted read-back reported `pricing_status: unpriced`,
142	  `unknown_model` for the configured model). Tokens, model and provider are shown correctly. Use the ledger for money:
143	  `python -m agentforge.operations.business_metrics`.
144	- The `agentforge.*` labels are sent but the hosted read-back API does not list them; check the dashboard's span detail to see
145	  whether it shows them. Status, error type, session, end user, tool name, model and tokens are shown by the read-back.
146	- The dashboard's trace-link format is not documented by Neatlogs, so the application records the **trace id** (worker log
147	  and the root span) rather than building URLs.
148	- Provider retries are counted for the OpenAI-compatible adapter (`on_attempt_failed`); a model adapter that does not offer
149	  the hook is traced without a retry count.
150	- Content mode redaction is pattern based. Metadata mode is the only mode with a hard guarantee (an allowlist).
151	- No hosted trace has been produced from this repository by the code change itself; that evidence comes from running it with
152	  a project key (see `docs/hackathon.md`).
153

# The agent

One loop serves every message: the model gets the conversation, a system prompt and its tools; it calls tools until it
has what it needs, then answers in plain text. That text is the answer, exactly as written
(`apps/api/src/agentforge/subagents/runtime.py`).

## What was removed, and why

Earlier versions ran a router, a planner, stage agents and an independent verifier, and forced every run to end by
submitting a typed result with evidence. A reply that did not satisfy those rules was rewritten as `PARTIAL`, so a
plain "What would you like help with?" showed a "Partial result" banner. All of that is gone: no router, planner,
verifier, `submit_result`, `PARTIAL` status or run-details page. A run ends as:

| Outcome | When | Shown |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `COMPLETED` | the model answered | its text, as written |
| `FAILED` | the provider or a tool broke | the reason: a provider's own message, credentials removed |
| `CANCELLED` | the person pressed Stop | "Stopped." |

Older messages may still carry `PARTIAL`; they render as plain text.

## Limits

Nothing caps steps, tool calls, cost or time. Usage is still recorded for accounting, and Stop always works. The
numbers in the budget rows (`Budget`, `UNLIMITED_*`) exist because the ledger needs positive values; they are set
high enough never to refuse anything.

## Tools

| Group | Tools |
| --- | --- |
| Web | `web_search`, `fetch_webpage` |
| Repository (read only, pinned commit) | `list_repo_files`, `search_repo`, `read_repo_file`, `get_issue`, `get_pr_status` |
| Sandbox (needs `E2B_API_KEY`) | `bash`, `read`, `write`, `edit`, `grep`, `find`, `ls` |
| Pull request (needs GitHub App + `ENABLE_GITHUB_WRITES`) | `create_pull_request` |
| Files and history | `create_task_artifact`, `read_task_artifact`, `search_conversation_history`, `read_context_resource` |
| Skills (when the person has any switched on) | `use_skill`: loads a playbook by name; see [skills](skills.md) |
| Plugins (per conversation) | `slug__tool`, from the MCP servers the person connected; see [plugins](plugins.md) |

The sandbox (`integrations/e2b_sandbox.py`, `tools/sandbox_shell.py`) is created on first use and kept for the
conversation: files and installed packages stay between messages. It has internet access and holds no secrets. When a
repository is selected the backend uploads its pinned commit and commits it as `agentforge-base`; pull requests are opened
by the backend from `git diff agentforge-base`, so GitHub credentials never enter the sandbox.

## Approvals

A global setting (`GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/approval-mode`, default `ask`) applies to every conversation.

* **Ask me**: before `bash`, `write`, `edit` or `create_pull_request` the run stops and the chat shows an Approve /
  Decline card (`approval.required`) with exactly what will run: the whole command, the file content or the edit, or
  the pull request with every file it changes. It waits as long as it takes. Declining returns a normal tool result
  telling the agent the person said no. A command too long to show in full is refused before anyone is asked.
* **Approve for me**: nothing asks.

A plugin tool also asks in **Ask me** mode unless its server declares it read-only.

The mode is read before each call, so switching it releases a waiting card. Answers: `POST /api/v1/tool-approvals/{id}`.
Implementation: `tools/approvals.py`, hooked into `tools/gateway.py`.
=====SUBAGENTS
# Delegated assignments

The default assistant (immutable `builtin/agent` version 3) can call
`delegate_task` with a short `title`, a self-contained `prompt`, and an optional
`mode` (`research` by default, or `work`). Existing tasks pinned to versions 1
and 2 retain their original definitions.

Delegation is synchronous, and independent assignments run in parallel. When the
main agent calls `delegate_task` several times in one reply, the children start
together and the agent receives every report once all have finished, in the order
it asked for them; it then verifies and integrates them. A reply that also calls
`bash`, `write` or `edit` stays strictly in order, as before. The tool description
is what teaches the model to launch independent assignments together (the agent
prompt is an immutable version). Work assignments share one workspace, so the
model is told to give parallel ones different files; `write` replaces a whole file,
so two children writing the same path would overwrite each other. A child that
fails or times out hands back its last few progress notes (`progress_notes`) so the
parent can build on its work. The child uses the configured model in a
separate conversation containing its assignment, platform instructions, and
authorized environment information. Parent messages are not automatically
copied. The conversation workspace and task-owned resources remain shared.

Research assignments cannot write files or execute commands. Work assignments
can use those tools only within the parent's grants, with the same approval
policy. Neither mode can delegate again or invoke `create_pull_request`.
The parent tool allowlist is a ceiling even when the packaged child definition
contains more tools. Settings' existing custom research agents retain their
current tool restrictions.

Each parent can create at most eight children, which is also the most that can
work at once. Each child has at most 40 model
operations, 80 tool operations, 600 seconds, and $5 in configured usage bounds,
further narrowed by inherited limits. These limits do not change the main
conversation's existing behavior. Model retries retain usage accounting through
the telemetry wrapper. Actual provider invoices can differ from configured cost
estimates.

## Persistence and recovery

Migration `0015_delegated_runs` adds the parent link, assignment title and prompt
to `agent_runs`, and permits child reservations at depth 2. Apply migrations
before restarting the API and worker. Downgrade refuses to remove depth-2 support
while child reservations remain; it does not discard historical records.

The child ID is derived from the parent tool operation identity. A task-locked
reservation transaction admits siblings of the running parent (counting ones whose
run row is not written yet, so a burst cannot pass the limit of eight) and rejects
unauthorized parents and any other active run.
The child owns its model/tool charges; the delegation adapter adds no second
charge. Both runs settle on cancellation. Existing worker lease supervision and
reconciliation preserve ambiguous outcomes without replaying external effects.
An uncertain child action stops the parent instead of suggesting a blind retry.

## Inspection

Each assignment is a card in the conversation, where it was started: title, status,
a running clock, step count and what the subagent is doing now. Subagents that stand
together get a heading ("3 subagents Â· 2 working"). The card needs no request of its
own: the delegation's `tool.started` event carries `child_run_id`, and the child's
events (which carry `parent_run_id`) update the card without appearing as steps of
the main run or in its counts. A subagent's Approve / Decline card is labelled with
its assignment (`approval.required` carries `agent_run_id`), and its card says it is
waiting. Runs recorded before this have neither field and show a plain card.
Opening a card reads
`GET /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}/tool-calls/{tool_call_id}/subagent`, with task and
project ownership enforced. It shows the assignment, child notes and tool
activity, terminal status, duration, and saved report. While open and running,
it refreshes every 1.5 seconds; closing aborts the request. Failed reads retain
the last result and offer Retry.

Child events keep their original task sequence and carry a parent marker.
They appear inside the assignment instead of duplicating the main timeline or
its counts. The detail response is bounded to the latest 200 events and marks
truncation. Reports remain on the run; large tool results are stored as context
resources before the parent receives a bounded preview.

## Verification

`scripts/release_checks.py` includes `apps/api/examples/subagent_smoke.py`.
The disposable PostgreSQL fixture exercises real run persistence, the model
loop, tool gateway, child results, owner isolation, declined writes, cancellation,
usage limits, and crash reconciliation without live provider effects.

Unit coverage lives in `test_delegation.py`, `test_telemetry_wrappers.py`, and
`activity-subagents.test.mjs`. Browser verification should cover desktop/mobile,
light/dark themes, keyboard disclosure, transient errors, and live updates.
Hosted rollout and real external workspace operations need their own environment
qualification; a local arithmetic delegation does not validate those services.

# Sandbox usage and cost evidence

`business_metrics` exports schema v2. It separates adapter-reported costs, configured-rate estimates, authorized upper bounds,
and unmeasured operations. A non-null ledger amount is not automatically a measured charge. Reports include cohort counts, daily
totals, distributions, and conservative cost per successful task, including failed-attempt costs. They never expose prompts,

E2B sends signed lifecycle events to `/api/v1/sandbox-usage/webhook`. Set `E2B_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (a dedicated signature secret of at least 32 characters; without it the webhook is unavailable) and subscribe to created,
resumed, paused, killed, updated, and checkpointed events. Receipt IDs deduplicate delivery retries. Only whitelisted metadata is
stored. API reconciliation accepts the provider's camelCase envelope as well as the documented webhook snake_case envelope.

```sh
cd apps/api
# Read-only preview of retained provider events:
.venv/bin/python -m agentforge.operations.reconcile_sandbox_usage --days 7

  --external-costs /private/assumptions.json --output /private/agentforge-costs.json

execution once, including idle-running time. Missing terminal events, missing rates, provider retention, and active intervals
remain explicit gaps. A zero plugin ledger amount does not prove the service is free. Neither ledger estimates nor lifecycle

I went through the AgentForge repo: README, the docs for the agent, sub-agents, plugins and Neatlogs, `docs/hackathon.md`, the git history, the `.entire/` config and logs, and the CFO.ai catalog entry. I also read the neatHack page. I didn't change any files.

## What you've actually built (what the demo can honestly claim)

| Area | What exists in the code |
|---|---|
| **The agent** | One agent loop with web search and page fetching, a read-only view of the repo at a pinned commit, and a persistent E2B sandbox per conversation (bash, read, write, edit). The sandbox holds no secrets. The agent can hand work to up to 8 parallel sub-agents (`delegate_task`), each shown as its own card. There are **Ask me** approval cards that show the exact command, edit or PR. Draft PRs are opened by the backend, so GitHub credentials never enter the sandbox. Every task has a usage ledger. |
| **Neatlogs** | Done properly ([telemetry/neatlogs_setup.py](../AgentForge/apps/api/src/agentforge/telemetry/neatlogs_setup.py)). Each task is one trace and each conversation is one session. Spans cover model calls (tokens, retries), every tool call (ERROR status plus its error code), nested sub-agents, approvals and refusals (as guardrail spans) and context preparation. By default only metadata is sent. It was checked against your hosted project on 12 Oct: one run hit 2× `FETCH_COMPRESSED_CONTENT_REJECTED` failures and still finished. |
| **cfo.ai** | It's an OAuth MCP plugin in the AgentForge catalog ([catalog.py:44](../AgentForge/apps/api/src/agentforge/plugins/catalog.py:44)), so AgentForge's own agent can build models inside CFO.ai. `business_metrics` exports your real cost per task. |
| **Entire** | Checkpoints are stored in git refs, and you have 1 Claude Code checkpoint out of 48 commits. |

## Fix these before you record

1. **The Entire overview's headline is "Stop capturing Claude Code sessions with Entire."** Ashish's latest commit (`f4580ee`) removed the Entire hooks. Two of the five judges are from Entire, and that's the first thing they'll see. Turn capture back on for one real fix session (the commit used `entire agent remove claude-code`, so `entire agent add claude-code` is probably the reverse). The commit from that session then becomes the headline, with a checkpoint attached.
2. **There's no Neatlogs before/after yet, and this is the biggest scoring gap.** Your Neatlogs dashboard already gives you the "before": 13.7% errors. The cause is real. In [safe_fetch.py:167](../AgentForge/apps/api/src/agentforge/integrations/safe_fetch.py:167), `fetch_webpage` sends `Accept-Encoding: identity`, but some sites send gzip anyway, and the agent then throws the page away. The same check exists in the Exa and Tavily clients. The loop to run:
   - Run 5 fixed prompts with `NEATLOGS_TAGS=baseline`.
   - In Claude Code, with the Neatlogs MCP and Entire both on, ask it to find the cause from the trace.
   - Fix it with bounded gzip/deflate decompression (cap the decompressed size).
   - Re-run the same 5 prompts with `NEATLOGS_TAGS=improved` and record the numbers.

   That one session gives you footage for both Neatlogs and Entire.
3. **Neatlogs shows "traces stopped flowing."** Make sure the worker you record with has `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` set. Set `NEATLOGS_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true` only for the demo task (it shows inputs and responses), and check that trace for secrets before you show it.
4. **Neatlogs spend shows $0.00006.** That's because it doesn't have a price for `gpt-6-luna`. Don't linger on that tile; your ledger is the real cost figure.
5. **The cfo.ai model doesn't exist yet.** Connect CFO.ai on AgentForge's Plugins page, give the agent the `business_metrics` JSON, and have it build the pricing and runway model. Then the agent planned its own business.
6. **Building in public is 15%.** Post on X with #neatHack today: the Neatlogs error screenshot, the fix, and the before/after numbers.

## The story

**"Trust needs three things: it can't break anything, you approve what matters, and you can see every step afterwards."** That's the hackathon's own tagline turned into your product. Neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai then come in as the way you *built, improved and planned* AgentForge, which is the wording of the 25% criterion.

## Demo script (target 2:50; the limit is 3:00)

Values in `[brackets]` are numbers you'll measure. Don't record until they're real.

**0:00–0:15: Hook**
*Screen:* the landing page at agentforge.vexelityai.com, then a new chat.
> "neatHack asked for agents you'd trust to run without watching. Trust takes three things: the agent can't break anything, you approve what matters, and you can see every step after. That's AgentForge."

**0:15–1:10: The agent (30%)**
*Screen:* a small public repo with a real bug and a failing test. Select the repo, choose **Ask me**, and type: *"Issue #1: [bug]. Find the cause, fix it, prove it with tests, open a draft PR."*
Then show, in order:
- the sub-agent cards ("3 subagents · 2 working")
- the sandbox `bash` test run failing
- the approval card showing the exact edit, then click Approve
- the tests passing
- the PR approval card listing the changed files
- the draft PR on GitHub

Put a "sped up 4×" label on screen.
> "I give it a real issue on a real repo, in Ask me mode. It reads the code at a pinned commit, then splits the work: three sub-agents investigate in parallel, each with its own card and report. It runs the tests in its own E2B sandbox, which holds no secrets. They fail. It finds the cause, and before changing a single file it stops and shows me the exact edit. I approve. Tests pass. Then the pull request: every changed file is listed before it opens, and our backend opens it, so GitHub credentials never enter the sandbox. Plan, tools, failure, fix, verification, delivery. Start to finish."

**1:10–1:55: Neatlogs**
*Screen:*
- The hero task's trace: the span tree, then `tool_approval` (guardrail) and `delegate_task` with the sub-agent nested under it.
- Neatlogs home showing **13.7%** errors.
- The failure trace: `fetch_webpage` ERROR, and the root span COMPLETED with `tool_failures=2`.
- Claude Code with the Neatlogs MCP pointing at `safe_fetch.py`.
- The baseline and improved runs side by side.

> "Every run is a Neatlogs trace, and every conversation is a session: model calls with tokens, each tool call, sub-agents nested under their parent, and my approvals as guardrail spans. Only metadata leaves our worker by default. Neatlogs showed a 13.7% error rate. The top error was FETCH_COMPRESSED_CONTENT_REJECTED: sites ignoring our no-compression header, so research pages were thrown away. The agent recovered, but it was half blind. Claude Code read that trace through the Neatlogs MCP and found the line. We added bounded decompression and re-ran the same tasks: errors went from 13.7 to [Y] percent, and tokens per task from [A] to [B]."

**1:55–2:20: Entire**
*Screen:* the fix commit in Entire, with the orange Claude Code checkpoint. Open it to show the prompt, the transcript and the diff. If you run it, show `entire graph` output for the fetch path.
> "That fix was written with Entire capturing the session. The commit carries its checkpoint (the prompt, the reasoning and the diff), so my teammate reviews why, not just what. [entire-graph showed us everything that touches the fetch path, so a security-sensitive fix didn't break the network guardrails.]"

**2:20–2:45: cfo.ai**
*Screen:* the Plugins page with CFO.ai connected, then a chat where the agent calls `cfo-ai__…` tools, then the model in CFO.ai: price, cost per task, margin, runway, and the base and downside scenarios.
> "Then the business. CFO.ai is a plugin inside AgentForge, with OAuth and approvals like any other tool. We exported our real cost per task from the usage ledger and asked AgentForge to build its own plan in CFO.ai: $[P] a month, [G]% gross margin at [C] customers, and [R] months of runway in the downside case. Measured costs, labelled assumptions."

**2:45–2:55: Close**
*Screen:* the architecture diagram from the README, the repo URL, the live URL and #neatHack.
> "AgentForge: hand off the task, keep the control, see every step. Live at agentforge.vexelityai.com, open source on GitHub."

## Recording tips
- The voiceover is about 440 words, which is about 2:55 at a normal pace. If you run long, trim the Entire graph line first.
- Record each section as a separate take and cut out waiting time. Label anything sped up or set up beforehand, as your own `hackathon.md` says to.
- Before publishing, check every frame for `.env` values, API keys and Neatlogs content-mode prompts.
- Submissions open at 7:00 PM IST today and are planned to close at 11:55 PM. You submit by quote-posting the official neatlogs post with your team, project, repo and demo link.

**Screenshots I'd find useful:** the Neatlogs trace detail for the failing run (the span tree), and AgentForge's sub-agent and approval cards during a real run. With those I can tighten the on-screen directions.

Should I write the bounded-decompression fix for `safe_fetch.py` and the Exa/Tavily clients? It's best done in a Claude Code session opened in the AgentForge repo with Entire turned back on, so the checkpoint becomes your demo footage.

content.text:
I did what I could from here. Nothing is committed or pushed. The most useful result: your own data gives a better Neatlogs story than the one in my first script.

## What your real data shows

From your Neatlogs project (via its API) and your local database (read-only queries):

| Finding | Number |
|---|---|
| `fetch_webpage` calls that failed | **22 of 39 (56%)**: 13 `FETCH_HTTP_ERROR`, 5 `SCOPE_DENIED`, 3 `FETCH_COMPRESSED_CONTENT_REJECTED`, 1 too large |
| Times the agent retried the **exact same failing URL** in one task | **4, and all 4 failed again**, in 3 tasks |
| Example hosted trace `6714884f…` | fetch ERROR after 162 ms; 4 model calls, **29,947 tokens in, 198 out** |
| Token mix over 7 days | **1.54M input vs 16k output**: about 99% of tokens are context |

I tested why the fetches fail:
- **Bot walls.** npm, Stack Overflow, Medium, G2 and Indeed return 403 even to a normal browser user-agent. Changing headers won't fix that, and you shouldn't try to get around it.
- **The real agent bug is how it recovers.** It retries a URL that just failed instead of using the search results it already has. That fits the hackathon's "Recovery" focus area exactly.
- **Compression is the second, smaller fix.** Some servers send gzip even when the agent asks for uncompressed pages.

## What I changed in `C:\Coding\AgentForge`

1. **Re-installed the Entire hooks for Claude Code** (`entire agent add claude-code`). This changes `.claude/settings.json` and undoes Ashish's commit `f4580ee`. Check with Ashish before pushing, in case he removed them for privacy.
2. **Added `.mcp.json`** so Claude Code connects to the Neatlogs MCP. It reads the key from an environment variable, so no secret is in the file. I checked that the endpoint answers with your key: it offers 26 tools, including `search_traces`, `get_project_analytics`, `triage_*` and `create_detection`.
3. **Updated `docs/hackathon.md`.** It no longer mentions entire-graph; Entire is described as checkpoints only, and CFO.ai as a plugin.
4. **Updated `docs/neatlogs.md`.** It now says the MCP is configured and checked.

I didn't write the fix itself. If I did it from here, Entire wouldn't capture it, because this session runs in the farmleaf folder. It needs its own session in AgentForge so the checkpoint becomes your demo footage.

## What you do next

**1. Make the Neatlogs key available to Claude Code.** This copies it from `.env` without displaying it. Restart the Claude app afterwards.
```powershell
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('NEATLOGS_API_KEY', ((Get-Content C:\Coding\AgentForge\.env | Select-String '^NEATLOGS_API_KEY=').Line -replace "^NEATLOGS_API_KEY=['""]?|['""]?$",''), 'User')
```

**2. Record the baseline.** Start the local worker with `NEATLOGS_TAGS=baseline`. Run each of these prompts in a new conversation:
1. `Open https://www.npmjs.com/package/react and tell me the latest version and weekly downloads.`
2. `Summarise the top answer at https://stackoverflow.com/questions/38987 in 3 bullets.`
3. `Read https://openai.com/api/pricing/ and list the per-million-token prices.`
4. `Fetch https://www.g2.com/products/linear/reviews and summarise what reviewers complain about.`
5. `Summarise https://docs.astral.sh/uv/ in 5 bullets.` (a control that should pass)

**3. Open a new Claude Code session in `C:\Coding\AgentForge`** and paste this prompt:

> Use the neatlogs MCP. Search the traces tagged `baseline` in workflow `agentforge-ai` and get project analytics for `fetch_webpage` failures. Then fix what they show:
> 1. **The agent repeats failed calls.** In `apps/api/src/agentforge/tools/gateway.py`, if a call in the same task has the same tool and args digest as one that already failed with a non-transient code, don't run it again. Non-transient means: `FETCH_HTTP_ERROR` for 4xx only (check how it separates 4xx from 5xx/429), `FETCH_COMPRESSED_CONTENT_REJECTED`, `SCOPE_DENIED`, `FETCH_RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE`. Return the original code with a short note: it already failed, so use another source, such as the search result content through `read_research_source`. Keep it as an ERROR tool span so Neatlogs shows it.
> 2. **Compressed pages.** In `apps/api/src/agentforge/integrations/safe_fetch.py:167`, decode gzip/deflate with a decompressed-size cap equal to `max_bytes`, so it's safe against zip bombs. Keep rejecting other encodings. Do the same in `exa_client.py` and `tavily_client.py`.
> 3. Use `create_detection` to add a Neatlogs detection for "same tool, same arguments, failed twice in one trace", if the tool supports it.
>
> Add tests, run them, and make one commit.

**4. Record the improved run.** Restart the worker with `NEATLOGS_TAGS=improved` and run the same 5 prompts. Compare failed fetches, repeated calls, tokens and duration per trace. Those are the before/after numbers for the video.

## Updated Neatlogs voiceover (replaces my first version)

> "Neatlogs showed us more than half our page fetches failed: 22 of 39. Worse, the agent kept retrying a URL that had already failed, and every retry failed again. Claude Code read those traces through the Neatlogs MCP, found the cause in our tool gateway, and fixed how the agent recovers. Same five tasks, before and after: failed fetches went from [X] to [Y], and tokens per task from [A] to [B]. And we turned the bug into a Neatlogs detection, so it can't come back quietly."

## Inputs for cfo.ai

These come from 18 local tasks, so label them as a small sample:
- Conservative cost per **successful** task (includes failed attempts): **$0.10**
- Median task: **$0.011**
- 95th percentile task: **$0.157**

The export also counts 9 of the 18 tasks as partial, an older status, and none failed. The JSON is in my scratchpad as `agentforge-costs-local.json`.

Your hosted server will have more data: run `business_metrics` there. On your local machine, the full export command fails until you run `alembic upgrade head`, because your local database is at migration `0019`. I didn't migrate it.

> "Here's our measured cost per task: [paste JSON]. Build a model in CFO.ai with a Free tier and a Pro tier, base and downside scenarios, gross margin and 12-month runway. Label every assumption."

It isn't set yet. Here's what it's for and how to do it.

## What it's for

The `.mcp.json` I pushed tells Claude Code: "connect to the Neatlogs MCP server and log in with `${NEATLOGS_API_KEY}`." That gives Claude Code tools to read your Neatlogs traces directly, like `search_traces` and `get_trace_context`. In the fix session you can then just ask: "look at my failing traces and find the cause."

The key isn't written in `.mcp.json`, because that file is on GitHub and would leak it. Claude Code reads it from a Windows environment variable called `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`. Right now that variable doesn't exist, so the Neatlogs connection would fail to log in.

## How to set it (2 minutes)

**1.** Open PowerShell, the normal Windows one. Run this, as a single line:
```powershell
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('NEATLOGS_API_KEY', ((Get-Content C:\Coding\AgentForge\.env | Select-String '^NEATLOGS_API_KEY=').Line -replace "^NEATLOGS_API_KEY=['""]?|['""]?$",''), 'User')
```
It copies the key from your AgentForge `.env` into a Windows user variable. It doesn't print the key anywhere.

**2. Fully quit the Claude app.** Closing the window isn't enough: right-click the Claude icon in the taskbar tray and choose Quit. Then open it again. Programs only pick up new environment variables when they start.

**3. Start a new Claude Code session with the folder set to `C:\Coding\AgentForge`.** The connection only exists in that folder, because `.mcp.json` lives there.

**4. Check it works.** In that new session:
- If Claude Code asks whether to trust or enable the `neatlogs` MCP server from `.mcp.json`, choose **Allow**.
- Type: `Use the neatlogs MCP whoami tool.` It should answer with your Neatlogs project. If it does, you're connected.

## If it doesn't connect

- **It says unauthorized, or `whoami` fails:** the app didn't pick up the variable. Make sure you fully quit it, not just closed the window.
- **The neatlogs server isn't listed at all:** the session isn't opened in `C:\Coding\AgentForge`.
- If it still fails, tell me what it says and I'll check the variable from here.

Once `whoami` works, you're ready for the baseline runs and then the fix session.

# Run the API, the worker and the web app together with prefixed output. Ctrl-C stops all three.
# Usage: scripts/dev.sh
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
if command -v corepack >/dev/null 2>&1; then PNPM="corepack pnpm"; else PNPM="pnpm"; fi
pids=()

# Each process gets its own process group, so stopping it also stops whatever it spawned (uvicorn reloader, next).
start() {
  local name="$1" directory="$2"; shift 2
  set -m
  ( cd "$ROOT/$directory" && "$@" 2>&1 | while IFS= read -r line; do printf '[%s] %s\n' "$name" "$line"; done ) &
  pids+=("$!")
  set +m
}

stop() {
  trap - INT TERM EXIT
  echo "Stopping..."
  for pid in "${pids[@]}"; do kill -TERM -- "-$pid" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null; done
  wait 2>/dev/null
  exit "${1:-0}"
}

"""Run the fixed Neatlogs evaluation prompts against the local AgentForge API, one conversation each.

Usage: python run_eval.py <label> <env-file> <out.json>
The bootstrap token is read from the env file and never printed.
"""
import json, sys, time, uuid
from pathlib import Path
import httpx

PROMPTS = [
    "Open https://www.npmjs.com/package/react and tell me the latest version and weekly downloads.",
    "Summarise the top answer at https://stackoverflow.com/questions/38987 in 3 bullets.",
    "Read https://openai.com/api/pricing/ and list the per-million-token prices.",
    "Fetch https://www.g2.com/products/linear/reviews and summarise what reviewers complain about.",
    "Summarise https://docs.astral.sh/uv/ in 5 bullets.",
]
TERMINAL = {"COMPLETED", "FAILED", "CANCELLED", "PARTIAL"}

label, env_file, out = sys.argv[1], Path(sys.argv[2]), Path(sys.argv[3])
token = next(l.split("=", 1)[1].strip().strip("'\"") for l in env_file.read_text().splitlines()
             if l.startswith("LOCAL_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN="))
api = httpx.Client(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8000", timeout=60)
r = api.post("/api/v1/auth/session", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"})
r.raise_for_status()
del token

results = []
for i, prompt in enumerate(PROMPTS, 1):
    s = api.post("/api/v1/sessions", json={"title": f"{label} eval {i}", "idempotency_key": str(uuid.uuid4())})
    s.raise_for_status()
    sid = s.json()["id"]
    t = api.post(f"/api/v1/sessions/{sid}/turns",
                 json={"routing": "auto", "idempotency_key": str(uuid.uuid4()), "goal": prompt})
    t.raise_for_status()
    start = time.time()
    status, task_id, turn = None, None, None
    while time.time() - start < 600:
        turns = api.get(f"/api/v1/sessions/{sid}/turns").json()
        turn = turns[-1] if turns else None
        task = (turn or {}).get("task") or {}
        task_id, status = task.get("id"), task.get("status")
        if status in TERMINAL:
            break
        time.sleep(3)
    answer = ((turn or {}).get("assistant_message") or {}).get("content") or ""
    results.append({"n": i, "prompt": prompt, "session_id": sid, "task_id": task_id, "status": status,
                    "seconds": round(time.time() - start, 1), "answer_preview": answer[:300]})
    print(f"[{label} {i}/5] {status} in {results[-1]['seconds']}s  task={task_id}", flush=True)

out.write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2))

"""Bind capability templates to concrete, server-authorized task resources."""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from uuid import UUID

from agentforge.contracts.agent_definition import AgentDefinition, Budget, Permissions, TOOL_CAPABILITIES, ToolName


class ScopeDenied(PermissionError):
    """A capability or a referenced resource is outside the current task."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TaskContext:
    """Internal service context; never deserialize this from model/tool arguments.

    Resource sets in every grant ceiling must be concrete. Context references
    are opaque immutable IDs validated by the application's resource resolver.
    """

    user_id: UUID
    project_id: UUID
    task_id: UUID
    platform_permissions: Permissions
    user_permissions: Permissions
    task_permissions: Permissions
    parent_permissions: Permissions
    platform_budget: Budget
    tier_budget: Budget
    task_budget: Budget
    parent_budget: Budget
    authorized_context_refs: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    depth: int = 0
    source_discovery_enabled: bool = False
    parent_run_id: UUID | None = None
    parent_tools: tuple[str, ...] | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EffectiveScope:
    permissions: Permissions
    allowed_tools: tuple[ToolName, ...]
    budget: Budget
    context_refs: tuple[str, ...]


def intersect_and_validate(
    definition: AgentDefinition, ctx: TaskContext, context_refs: tuple[str, ...],
) -> EffectiveScope:
    if ctx.depth not in (0, 1) or (ctx.depth == 1 and (ctx.parent_run_id is None or ctx.parent_tools is None)):
        raise ScopeDenied("nested sub-agent delegation is disabled")
    # Round-trip through JSON revalidates even models constructed with model_copy.
    definition = AgentDefinition.model_validate_json(definition.model_dump_json())
    ceilings = [Permissions.model_validate_json(p.model_dump_json()) for p in (
        ctx.platform_permissions, ctx.user_permissions, ctx.task_permissions, ctx.parent_permissions,
    )]
    values: dict[str, object] = {}
    for name in Permissions.model_fields:
        if name.startswith("allowed_"):
            grants = [getattr(p, name) for p in ceilings]

"""Immutable research persistence with fresh task/project ownership on every read."""

from collections.abc import Callable
import hashlib
from typing import Any
from uuid import UUID, uuid4

from sqlalchemy import func, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from agentforge.database.models import AgentRun, Project, Task
from agentforge.database.research_models import ResearchArtifact, ResearchEvidence, ResearchSource
from agentforge.subagents.scope import ScopeDenied, TaskContext


def _uuid(value: str | UUID) -> UUID:
    try:
        parsed = UUID(str(value))
        if str(parsed) != str(value):
            raise ValueError("noncanonical reference")
        return parsed
    except (ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError):
        raise ScopeDenied("invalid research reference") from None


class ResearchRepository:
    def __init__(self, session_factory: Callable[[], Session]) -> None:
        self.session_factory = session_factory

    @staticmethod
    def _owned(session: Session, *, task_id: UUID, owner_id: UUID, project_id: UUID) -> Task:
        task = session.scalar(select(Task).join(Project, Project.id == Task.project_id).where(
            Task.id == task_id, Task.project_id == project_id, Task.created_by == owner_id,
            Project.owner_id == owner_id))
        if task is None:
            raise ScopeDenied("research task ownership is not authorized")
        return task

    @staticmethod
    def _scope(ctx: TaskContext) -> dict[str, UUID]:
        return {"task_id": ctx.task_id, "owner_id": ctx.user_id, "project_id": ctx.project_id}

    @staticmethod
    def _writable(task: Task) -> None:
        if task.cancel_requested_at is not None or task.status in {"COMPLETED", "PARTIAL", "FAILED", "CANCELLED"}:
            raise ScopeDenied("research task no longer accepts new evidence")

    @staticmethod
    def _source(row: ResearchSource, *, full: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
        value = {"id": str(row.id), "task_id": str(row.task_id), "url": row.url,
    def add_source(self, ctx: TaskContext, *, run_id: UUID, operation_key: str, ordinal: int,
                   url: str, title: str, content: str, source_type: str,
                   fetch_status: str, error_code: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
        if len(content.encode()) > 2_000_000 or len(url) > 2048 or len(title) > 1000:
            raise ValueError("research_source_size_limit")
        with self.session_factory() as session, session.begin():
            self._writable(self._owned(session, **self._scope(ctx)))
            run = session.scalar(select(AgentRun.id).where(AgentRun.id == run_id, AgentRun.task_id == ctx.task_id))
            if run is None:
                raise ScopeDenied("research run is outside the task")
            existing = session.scalar(select(ResearchSource).where(ResearchSource.task_id == ctx.task_id,
                ResearchSource.operation_key == operation_key, ResearchSource.ordinal == ordinal))
            if existing is not None:
                if (existing.agent_run_id != run_id or existing.url != url or existing.title != title or
                    existing.content != content or existing.source_type != source_type or
                    existing.fetch_status != fetch_status or existing.error_code != error_code):
                    raise ScopeDenied("immutable source operation does not match its original inputs")
                return self._source(existing)
            row = ResearchSource(id=uuid4(), task_id=ctx.task_id, agent_run_id=run_id,
                operation_key=operation_key, ordinal=ordinal, url=url, title=title,
                content=content, content_sha256=hashlib.sha256(content.encode()).hexdigest(),
                source_type=source_type, fetch_status=fetch_status, error_code=error_code)
            session.add(row)
            session.flush()
            # Every source ID is independently acceptable as a source reference;
            # this evidence record records what retrieval actually establishes.
            session.add(ResearchEvidence(id=uuid4(), task_id=ctx.task_id, source_id=row.id,
                kind="source_retrieval", validation_state=fetch_status,
                evidence_json={"content_sha256": row.content_sha256, "fetch_status": fetch_status}))
            return self._source(row)

    def list_sources(self, *, task_id: UUID, owner_id: UUID, project_id: UUID) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        with self.session_factory() as session:
            self._owned(session, task_id=task_id, owner_id=owner_id, project_id=project_id)
            rows = session.execute(select(*self._preview_columns()).where(
                ResearchSource.task_id == task_id).order_by(ResearchSource.retrieved_at, ResearchSource.id).limit(1000)).mappings()
            return [self._source_preview(row) for row in rows]

    def read_source(self, source_id: str, *, task_id: UUID, owner_id: UUID, project_id: UUID) -> dict[str, Any]:
        with self.session_factory() as session:
            self._owned(session, task_id=task_id, owner_id=owner_id, project_id=project_id)
            row = session.scalar(select(ResearchSource).where(ResearchSource.id == _uuid(source_id),
                                                            ResearchSource.task_id == task_id))
            if row is None:
                raise ScopeDenied("source reference is outside the task")
            return self._source(row, full=True)

    def sources_for_url(self, ctx: TaskContext, url: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        with self.session_factory() as session:
            self._owned(session, **self._scope(ctx))
            rows = session.execute(select(*self._preview_columns()).where(
                ResearchSource.task_id == ctx.task_id, ResearchSource.url == url,
                ResearchSource.fetch_status.in_(("SEARCH_ONLY", "FETCHED"))).order_by(ResearchSource.retrieved_at).limit(1000)).mappings()
            return [self._source_preview(row) for row in rows]

    def verify_references(self, ctx: TaskContext, *, evidence_ids: tuple[str, ...], artifact_ids: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
        with self.session_factory() as session:
            self._owned(session, **self._scope(ctx))

# A web address as people paste it into a message; trailing sentence punctuation is trimmed below.
_MESSAGE_URL = re.compile(r"https?://[^\s<>\"'`]+", re.IGNORECASE)
_TRAILING = ".,;:!?*_'\""
_CLOSERS = {")": "(", "]": "[", "}": "{", ">": "<"}
MAX_MESSAGE_URLS = 20


def normalized_url(url: str) -> str | None:
    """The form search results are stored in (`str(httpx.URL(...))`), or None for anything that is not a web address."""
    try:
        value = str(httpx.URL(url))
    except (httpx.InvalidURL, TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    parts = urlsplit(value)
    return value if parts.scheme in ("http", "https") and parts.hostname else None


def message_urls(text: str | None) -> frozenset[str]:
    """The exact web addresses written in a message, normalized, at most MAX_MESSAGE_URLS.

    A closing bracket stays only when the address opened it (Wikipedia-style "(disambiguation)" links), so
    "(see https://x.dev/a)." yields https://x.dev/a.
    """
    found: set[str] = set()
    for match in _MESSAGE_URL.finditer(text or ""):
        candidate = match.group(0)
        while candidate:
            last = candidate[-1]
            if last in _TRAILING or (last in _CLOSERS and candidate.count(_CLOSERS[last]) < candidate.count(last)):
                candidate = candidate[:-1]
            else:
                break
        url = normalized_url(candidate)
        if url is not None:
            found.add(url)
            if len(found) >= MAX_MESSAGE_URLS:
                break
    return frozenset(found)

The gateway does not count, cap or deduplicate calls: a model may repeat a call or make as many as it likes."""

REPO, SHA = "owner/name", "a" * 40
ALL = ("read_repo_file", "list_repo_files", "read", "write", "grep")


class FakeCalls:
    def __init__(self):
        self.intents, self.outcomes = [], {}

    def record_intent(self, **kwargs):
        call_id = uuid4()
        self.intents.append((call_id, kwargs))
        return call_id

    def record_outcome(self, *, call_id, status, result_json=None, error_code=None, evidence_ids=()):
        self.outcomes[call_id] = {"status": status, "result_json": result_json, "error_code": error_code}

    def last(self):
        return list(self.outcomes.values())[-1]


class FakeBudgets:
    def __init__(self):
        self.usage = []

    def check_active(self, reservation_id): pass

    def authorize_operation(self, *args, **kwargs): pass

    def record_usage(self, reservation_id, key, cost, usage=None):
        self.usage.append(cost)


class FakeResources:
    def __init__(self, bound=None):
        self.bound = {"repo_id": REPO, "ref": SHA} if bound is None else bound

    def bindings(self, ctx, name):
        return self.bound

    async def verify_tool_inputs(self, ctx, name, args): pass

    async def verify_references(self, ctx, *, evidence_ids, artifact_ids): pass


def ok(**data):
    return ToolOutcome(status="ok", data=data, cost_usd=Decimal(0))


def make(handlers=None, *, bound=None):
    handlers = handlers or {}
    catalog = ToolCatalog()
    for name in ALL:
        async def default(args, ctx):
            return ok(echo=args.model_dump(mode="json"))
        catalog.register(name, handlers.get(name, default), max_cost_usd=Decimal(0), timeout_sec=5)
    calls, budgets = FakeCalls(), FakeBudgets()
    gateway = ToolGateway(
        catalog=catalog, calls=calls, budgets=budgets, resources=FakeResources(bound), reauthorize=AsyncMock(),
        ctx=NS(task_id=uuid4(), parent_run_id=None), scope=NS(allowed_tools=ALL, permissions=NS(), budget=Budget()),
        run_id=uuid4(), reservation_id=uuid4())
    return gateway, calls, budgets

"""A URL the person wrote can be fetched directly; a model-made URL still needs a search; failed fetches point at what is held.

Found with Neatlogs: in every baseline trace the first fetch_webpage call was refused (SCOPE_DENIED) because the page the
person had pasted had not come from a search yet, and a refused or blocked page sent the model into repeated searching.
"""
from types import SimpleNamespace as NS
from unittest import IsolatedAsyncioTestCase, TestCase
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, patch
from uuid import uuid4

from agentforge.repositories.research import MAX_MESSAGE_URLS, message_urls, normalized_url
from agentforge.subagents.resources import DatabaseResourceResolver
from agentforge.subagents.scope import ScopeDenied
from agentforge.tools.catalog import ERROR_GUIDANCE, TOOL_DESCRIPTIONS, error_guidance


class MessageUrlTests(TestCase):
    def test_addresses_are_found_as_people_write_them(self):
        text = ("Open https://www.npmjs.com/package/react, then (see https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). "
                "Also **https://example.com/a?b=1&c=2** and <https://example.org/x>.")
        self.assertEqual(message_urls(text), {
            "https://www.npmjs.com/package/react", "https://docs.astral.sh/uv/",
            "https://example.com/a?b=1&c=2", "https://example.org/x"})

    def test_a_bracket_the_address_opened_is_kept(self):
        self.assertEqual(message_urls("Read https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_(planet)."),
                         {"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_(planet)"})

    def test_addresses_are_normalized_like_search_results(self):
        self.assertEqual(message_urls("HTTPS://Example.COM"), {normalized_url("https://example.com")})
        self.assertEqual(normalized_url("https://example.com"), "https://example.com")

    def test_only_web_addresses_count_and_there_is_a_limit(self):
        self.assertEqual(message_urls("ftp://files.example.com/a and javascript:alert(1) and no links"), frozenset())
        self.assertEqual(message_urls(None), frozenset())
        many = " ".join(f"https://site{i}.example.com/" for i in range(MAX_MESSAGE_URLS + 5))
        self.assertEqual(len(message_urls(many)), MAX_MESSAGE_URLS)
        self.assertIsNone(normalized_url("not a url"))


class FakeRepository:
    def __init__(self, goal="", sources=()):
        self.goal, self.sources = goal, list(sources)

    def sources_for_url(self, ctx, url):
        return [s for s in self.sources if s["url"] == url and s["fetch_status"] in ("SEARCH_ONLY", "FETCHED")]

    def list_sources(self, **_):
        return self.sources

    def message_urls(self, ctx):
        return message_urls(self.goal)


def context(discovery=True):
    return NS(task_id=uuid4(), user_id=uuid4(), project_id=uuid4(), source_discovery_enabled=discovery)


def scope(hosts=()):
    return NS(permissions=NS(allowed_web_hosts=hosts))


class ResolverTests(IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    def resolver(self, **repository):
        return DatabaseResourceResolver(FakeRepository(**repository), NS(check_context=AsyncMock()))

    async def resolve(self, resolver, url, *, ctx=None, hosts=()):
        public = NS(url=url)
        with patch("agentforge.integrations.safe_fetch.resolve_public_url", AsyncMock(return_value=public)) as resolve:
            result = await resolver.resolve_web_url(ctx or context(), "fetch_webpage", NS(source_url=url), scope(hosts))
        return result, resolve

    async def test_a_url_the_person_wrote_is_fetched_without_a_search_first(self):
        resolver = self.resolver(goal="Open https://www.npmjs.com/package/react and tell me the version.")
        (public, hosts), resolve = await self.resolve(resolver, "https://www.npmjs.com/package/react")
        self.assertEqual(public.url, "https://www.npmjs.com/package/react")
        self.assertEqual(hosts, ("www.npmjs.com",))
        resolve.assert_awaited_once_with("https://www.npmjs.com/package/react", ("www.npmjs.com",))
        await resolver.verify_tool_inputs(context(), "fetch_webpage", NS(source_url="https://www.npmjs.com/package/react"))

    async def test_a_url_the_model_made_up_is_still_refused(self):
        resolver = self.resolver(goal="Open https://www.npmjs.com/package/react please.")
        for url in ("https://www.npmjs.com/package/react?leak=secret", "https://attacker.example/collect",
                    "https://www.npmjs.com/package/vue"):
            with self.subTest(url=url):
                with self.assertRaises(ScopeDenied):
                    await self.resolve(resolver, url)
                with self.assertRaises(ScopeDenied):
                    await resolver.verify_tool_inputs(context(), "fetch_webpage", NS(source_url=url))

    async def test_search_results_still_work_and_both_kinds_of_host_are_trusted(self):
        resolver = self.resolver(goal="Compare with https://docs.astral.sh/uv/",
            sources=[{"url": "https://pypi.org/project/uv/", "fetch_status": "SEARCH_ONLY"}])
        (_, hosts), _ = await self.resolve(resolver, "https://pypi.org/project/uv/")
        self.assertEqual(hosts, ("docs.astral.sh", "pypi.org"))

    async def test_task_host_limits_still_apply_to_a_typed_url(self):
        resolver = self.resolver(goal="Open https://www.npmjs.com/package/react")
        (_, hosts), resolve = await self.resolve(resolver, "https://www.npmjs.com/package/react", hosts=("docs.astral.sh",))
        self.assertEqual(hosts, ())  # the network layer then refuses the host
        (_, hosts), _ = await self.resolve(resolver, "https://www.npmjs.com/package/react", ctx=context(discovery=False))
        self.assertEqual(hosts, ())


class GuidanceTests(TestCase):
    def test_a_failed_fetch_points_at_the_search_results_already_held(self):
        for code in ("FETCH_HTTP_ERROR", "FETCH_CONTENT_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED", "FETCH_COMPRESSED_CONTENT_REJECTED"):
            guidance = error_guidance(code)
            self.assertIn("read_research_source", guidance)
            self.assertIn("Do not search for the same page again", guidance)

    def test_a_repeated_failed_call_has_its_own_guidance(self):
        self.assertIn("REPEATED_FAILED_CALL", ERROR_GUIDANCE)
        self.assertEqual(error_guidance("REPEATED_FAILED_CALL"), ERROR_GUIDANCE["REPEATED_FAILED_CALL"])

    def test_the_fetch_tool_says_a_written_url_can_be_opened(self):
        self.assertIn("A URL the person wrote in their message can be opened directly", TOOL_DESCRIPTIONS["fetch_webpage"])
